Path traversal vulnerability. The regex pattern at line 10 only checks for literal '../../' sequences, which can be bypassed using URL encoding (%2e%2e%2f), double encoding, or other techniques. User-controlled path from self.path is directly concatenated at line 14 and used in open() at line 22, allowing arbitrary file read from the filesystem.

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability. User-controlled URL from request.args.get('url') is fetched using urllib.request.urlopen(). The check at line 14 only verifies the URL starts with 'https://insecurewebapp.com', which can be bypassed using subdomains (e.g., https://insecurewebapp.com.attacker.com) or other techniques. This allows attackers to make the server send requests to arbitrary internal or external resources.

SSL/TLS hostname verification is disabled by setting context.check_hostname = False. This allows man-in-the-middle attacks as the client will not verify that the server's certificate matches the expected hostname. An attacker could present a valid certificate for a different domain and intercept the connection.

Hash length extension vulnerability. The signature is computed by concatenating secret + payment_information and hashing with SHA-256. This pattern is vulnerable to length extension attacks where an attacker can append additional data to payment_information and compute a valid signature without knowing the secret. Should use HMAC instead: hmac.new(secret, payment_information.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
